source_text: Quam mecum nihil egeris, litterarum omnium testatur eruditio; quam vero contra Apostolum nitaris, et contra Deum insanias, sententiarum tuarum pugna demonstrat. Sed ostenso iam, non posse haec coniungi, quae rerum natura dissociat; interrogemus et Apostolum, ne illius putetur inesse sensibus, quae in tuis est sententiis probata barbaries.
pass_a_gloss: How you have done nothing with me, the learning of all letters testifies; but how you strive against the Apostle, and rave against God, the fight of your sentences demonstrates. But, it having already been shown that these things cannot be joined which the nature of things dissociates; let us also question the Apostle, lest that barbarity which has been proved in your sentences be thought to be in his senses.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: All literary learning testifies that you have achieved nothing against me. The conflict between your statements shows how you struggle against the apostle and rage against God. But now that we have shown that things separated by their very nature cannot be joined, let us question the apostle too. Otherwise the barbarity proved to exist in your statements might be thought to exist in his understanding.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
